summary.intent: Investigate and fix the someguy v0.11.1 IPNS routing sidecar that was hanging indefinitely on staging, then validate the fix with E2E and load tests and deploy to staging.
summary.outcome: Someguy was fixed (wrong resource limits, missing libp2p port, wrong DHT mode), an API-level fallback to delegated-ipfs.dev with Prometheus metrics was implemented, staging deploy succeeded with all 83 SDK E2E tests passing and 15.28 ops/s throughput (12x improvement over Phase 18 baseline). A months-long release-please deadlock was also resolved as a side effect.

repo: someguy LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY env var expects raw uint64 bytes, not human-readable strings like '1GB' — the container silently crash-loops with 'could not parse 1GB as uint64'

release-please multi-package mode with include-component-in-tag:false is broken — it creates bare v{version} tags but its own scanner cannot re-match them to path '.'; fix is include-component-in-tag:true with an explicit component name
Staging pre-release tags in v{version}-staging-rc-N format polluted release-please's release scanner, causing it to match staging releases as root package releases and deadlock
The THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET was not wired into the staging deploy workflow, so it was lost on each deploy and rate-limiting blocked test runs
vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env — env vars must be passed explicitly via CLI or a setup file

The delegated routing client resolve flow always prefers the DB over the network because publishes are fire-and-forget and the DB is written synchronously first, meaning ~100% of resolves are DB-sourced by design
packages/crypto existed as an independent package but was missing from release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json, causing it to be versioned out of band
Someguy with a cold DHT is slower than delegated-ipfs.dev at median, but after 8 hours of warm-up it outperforms delegated-ipfs.dev on all metrics (15.28 vs 10.75 ops/s)

code.finding: backend parameter typed as string; should be 'primary' | 'fallback' literal union for type safety

resolveRecord() always queries DB after network and prefers whichever has higher sequence number. Since DB is written synchronously before fire-and-forget DHT publish, DB always wins — 100% of resolves are DB-sourced
publishRecord() publishes to delegated routing as fire-and-forget (detached promise) with comment 'DB is the reliable source' — this is intentional architecture, not a bug

workflow: release-please PR label autorelease:pending must be flipped to autorelease:tagged when manually creating a release tag, or future runs deadlock with 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding - aborting'
When release-please can't find a release for a package path, it walks the entire commit history (600+ commits) and may major-bump the version based on historical feat: commits
Creating an anchor GitHub Release with the correct tag format unblocks release-please without needing to modify the config — it just needs one matchable release to anchor to
Docker healthchecks run inside the container, not on the host — a healthcheck using wget may pass on the host while failing inside a minimal Go container that only ships curl
Staging Tauri desktop builds create GitHub Releases with the tag format, which pollutes release-please's release scanner if the tag format overlaps with the root package pattern
The deploy-staging workflow triggers on tag push independently of tag-staging-release — pushing a tag directly bypasses the E2E gate

friction: release-please include-component-in-tag:false is fundamentally broken in multi-package repos — creates tags it then cannot re-find, requiring multiple debug cycles spanning the entire session
Old staging release tags (v*-staging-rc-N) accumulated over months and polluted the release-please scanner, requiring manual bulk deletion of 29 releases before the root issue became clear
SSH to the staging VPS requires 1Password agent approval interactively, making unattended VPS checks impossible without user intervention
Vitest not auto-loading .env files caused confusing 429 rate limit failures that looked like throttler config issues until the root cause was found
Release-please labeling race condition: the PR is created before GitHub's internal graph resolves the node ID, causing the label-add step to fail with 'Could not resolve node global id'
The release-please 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding - aborting' error masked the real root cause (component matching failure) for most of the debugging session
1Password SSH agent repeatedly prompted for approval during the session, blocking automated VPS operations
open_items: mock-ipns-routing service is still in docker-compose.yml alongside someguy — intentionally kept for CI compatibility but adds clutter to local dev setup
DB-first IPNS resolution means 100% of resolves hit the database; shifting to network-first when sequence numbers match is a future optimization if DB load becomes a concern
someguy's SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS fanout feature (race to delegated-ipfs.dev in parallel) was evaluated but skipped — could provide best-of-both-worlds latency at the cost of complexity
Grafana alerting on cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total needs to be configured to surface frequent fallbacks to public infra
PR #335 (throttle bypass in deploy workflow) needs merge and inclusion in a release
PR #336 (Phase 19 someguy baselines doc) needs merge
The load test metrics JSON files were being committed accidentally — gitignore was added but existing committed files (if any) may need cleanup
